newsitem.title: MEXICO: Alleged Mexican druglord wins new reprieve - paper.
newsitem.headline: Alleged Mexican druglord wins new reprieve - paper.

text.p: One of Mexico's top alleged drug lords, Hector "The Blond" Palma, has won a reprieve from multiple murder charges in his latest courtroom victory this year, Reforma newspaper reported on Thursday.

It said that Palma, who remains in a maximum-security jail on drug and other charges, was cleared of the murder of nine members of a rival drug kingpin's family in 1992 -- a killing portrayed by the government as a mafia-style blood feud.

The decision was made on Wednesday by a judge in the city of Toluca, outside Mexico City, the newspaper said, but was subject to review by an appeals court. The attorney general's office had no immediate comment on the report.

Authorities charged Palma with abducting and murdering nine members of the family of his arch-enemy Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo in 1992 and dumping their bullet-riddled bodies in the southern Mexican state of Guerrero.

They said the killings were part of a merciless feud between Palma and Felix Gallardo after Palma deserted the latter's Tijuana cartel and set up his own cartel trafficking Colombian cocaine into the United States.

Police said Gallardo is supposed to have ordered a Venezuelan drug trafficker to seduce Palma's wife before killing her in San Francisco. They said the Venezuelan then took Palma's two children to Venezuela and threw them to their death off a bridge.

Palma, who was arrested in 1995 after his plane crashed in western Mexico, was cleared in June of another mass-slaying five years ago of five people in a beach-side disco. That was believed to have been an intended attack on Felix Gallardo's associates.
